raw_case_text: A 30-year-old woman (gravida 3, para 1) had fetal ascites detected at 22 GW by occasional ultrasound with the complaint of abdominal distension. Further investigation showed fetal pericardial effusion and positive CMV-IgM. Because of positive CMV-DNA in the amniotic fluid (3.4 x 106 copies/ml), she was transferred to our center for further treatment at 24 GW and 4 days. Fetal MRI at 30 weeks showed massive ascites, hepatomegaly, pericardial effusion, and compressed low-intensity lungs (Figure 2A). We performed fetal therapies, including intravenous immunoglobulin to the mother (24, 25, 26, and 30 GW), ascites removal followed by fetal intraperitoneal injection of immunoglobulin at 28 GW and albumin plus packed red blood cells at 29 GW to treat fetal anemia. At 31 GW and 2 days, she gave birth to a female neonate (birth weight, 2,236 g; Apgar scores of 1 and 1 at 1 and 5 min, respectively) via emergent cesarean section because of non-reassuring fetal status. The neonate was heavily edematous and had bradycardia at birth. Her condition was diagnosed as hydrops fetalis based on the generalized edema and massive ascites. She was resuscitated with manual ventilation under inhaled nitric oxide and chest compression. However, she did not respond to resuscitation and died 20 min after birth. A blood test showed leukocytosis (31,300/mul), anemia (41 g/l), thrombocytopenia (2.4 x 104/mul), hypogammaglobulinemia (1.51 g/l), hypoalbuminemia (6.0 g/l), and increased aspartate aminotransferase levels (650 IU/l). Abdominal echo revealed hepatomegaly with hyperechoic lesions suggesting hemorrhage in the liver, and brain echo revealed mild ventriculomegaly and hyperechoic lesions suggesting calcifications. Autopsy imaging showed pulmonary hypoplasia, hepatomegaly, ascites, and intracranial calcification (Figures 2B,C). Positive CMV-DNA (blood: 1.6 x 103 copies/106 white blood cells, tracheal aspirates: 4.5 x 104 copies/ml) confirmed congenital CMV infection.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 30-year-old pregnant woman (gravida 3, para 1) presented at 22 weeks' gestation with maternal abdominal distension and ultrasound findings of fetal ascites and pericardial effusion, delivering a hydropic preterm female neonate at 31 weeks 2 days' gestation.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Evaluated at 22 weeks' gestation for abdominal distension, the mother was found to have fetal ascites, fetal pericardial effusion, positive maternal CMV-IgM, and amniotic fluid CMV-DNA of 3.4 x 10^6 copies/mL, prompting transfer at 24 weeks 4 days. Despite maternal IVIG infusions (24, 25, 26, 30 GW) and fetal paracentesis with fetal intraperitoneal immunoglobulin (28 GW) and albumin plus packed RBC transfusion for fetal anemia (29 GW), non-reassuring fetal status at 31 weeks 2 days necessitated emergency cesarean delivery of a severely hydropic, bradycardic 2,236 g female neonate.
subjective.past_medical_history: Mother: 30-year-old gravida 3, para 1 with gestational CMV infection. Neonate: preterm female born at 31 weeks 2 days' gestation (birth weight 2,236 g) with congenital CMV hydrops fetalis.
subjective.review_of_systems: Maternal complaint of abdominal distension at 22 GW; neonatal generalized hydrops fetalis and severe birth asphyxia/bradycardia.

objective.physical_examination: Female neonate at birth (31w2d): birth weight 2,236 g, Apgar scores 1 at 1 min and 1 at 5 min; severe generalized edema, massive ascites (hydrops fetalis), and profound bradycardia unresponsive to resuscitation.
objective.routine_investigations: Maternal CMV-IgM positive. Neonatal blood tests at birth: leukocytosis (WBC 31,300/uL), severe anemia (hemoglobin 41 g/L), severe thrombocytopenia (platelets 2.4 x 10^4/uL), severe hypogammaglobulinemia (IgG 1.51 g/L), severe hypoalbuminemia (albumin 6.0 g/L), and elevated AST (650 IU/L). Neonatal abdominal ultrasound showed hepatomegaly with hyperechoic intrahepatic hemorrhagic lesions; cranial ultrasound showed mild ventriculomegaly and hyperechoic intracranial calcifications.
objective.advanced_workup: Amniocentesis PCR showed amniotic fluid CMV-DNA of 3.4 x 10^6 copies/mL. Fetal MRI at 30 GW demonstrated massive fetal ascites, hepatomegaly, pericardial effusion, and compressed low-intensity hypoplastic lungs. Neonatal CMV-DNA PCR was positive in blood (1.6 x 10^3 copies/10^6 WBCs) and tracheal aspirates (4.5 x 10^4 copies/mL). Postmortem autopsy imaging confirmed severe pulmonary hypoplasia, hepatomegaly, massive ascites, and intracranial calcifications.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Definitive diagnosis of fatal congenital cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection with non-immune hydrops fetalis, severe fetal/neonatal anemia and thrombocytopenia, hepatic hemorrhage, intracranial calcifications, and pulmonary hypoplasia, confirmed by amniotic fluid CMV-DNA (3.4 x 10^6 copies/mL), neonatal blood CMV-DNA (1.6 x 10^3 copies/10^6 WBCs), tracheal aspirate CMV-DNA (4.5 x 10^4 copies/mL), and postmortem imaging. Despite prenatal maternal IVIG and fetal intraperitoneal IVIG, albumin, and PRBC transfusions, the neonate did not respond to neonatal resuscitation with manual ventilation, inhaled nitric oxide, and chest compressions and died 20 minutes after birth.
